notes.content:

Instead, you’ll need to [b]clear alien nests[/b] to unlock upgrades and new weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]Survivor Mode also features [b]exclusive Orbital Strike weapons[/b] that can’t be found anywhere else.[/p][/*][*][p]And if you manage to survive long enough… the [b]final boss[/b] will appear. Beat it, and you’ve conquered the run.[/p][/*][/list][p]This mode is designed for those of you who wanted a faster, more action-packed experience, while Classic Mode remains for players who love the more strategic, colony-building gameplay.[/p][h3][b]Other Updates in Patch #3[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Bug fixes for stability and smoother play.[/p][/*][*][p]Quality-of-life improvements across the board.[/p][/*][*][p]UI, audio, and balance polish.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]A Note from Me[/b][/h3][p]I’m beyond excited to finally share Survivor Mode with you all. If you’re enjoying it, please consider [b]leaving a Steam review[/b]—it helps me out so much as a solo developer.[/p][p]And of course, come join us on [b]Discord[/b] to share your feedback, bug reports, and survivor stories. I can’t wait to hear what you think of the new mode![/p][p]See you out there,
Nima[/p]

notes.title: Patch #2 Release Notes - Full Controller Support + Smarter Enemies
notes.content:
[b]Full Controller Support + Smarter Enemies[/b]

[b]Controller Support[/b]
[list]
[*] Full support for PlayStation and Xbox controllers has been added.
[*] The entire game is now fully playable on Steam Deck.
[*] All menus, UI, and in-game systems have been updated to work seamlessly with controller input.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Enemies now react more intelligently when attacked, improving the flow and feel of combat.
[*] Behavior adjustments lead to more dynamic engagements, especially in mid- to late-game waves.
[*] Enemy Balance Tweaks
[*] Slight increases to enemy health across various types.
[/list]
These changes are aimed at making combat more satisfying and a bit more challenging, especially for experienced players.

More improvements are in the works, and your feedback continues to shape every update. If you haven’t already, join us in the Discord to share your thoughts or report any issues. Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Patch #1 - Release Notes
notes.content:
The first major patch is here! This update focuses on expanding gameplay with new upgrade systems, polishing existing features, improving UI and audio feedback, and fixing bugs based on community feedback.

We’re also incredibly excited to release the official soundtrack as a DLC, featuring music by world-renowned electronic producer [b]Joel Mull[/b]. The music has been a core part of the game’s atmosphere from the start, and now you can enjoy it outside the game as well. Huge thanks to Joel for crafting such a powerful and immersive soundscape!

Thank you to everyone who’s played and supported the game since launch!

[h3]New Feature: Building Upgrade Station[/h3]
The Building Upgrade Station is now active. You can spend Crystals mined during your runs to unlock permanent meta-upgrades that strengthen your colonies across future playthroughs.

[h3]New upgrades include:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Alpha-7 Droid – A powerful new droid unit assembled at the Droid Factory.
[*] Shield Domes – Add protective shielding to your turrets.
[*] Improved Power Plants – Increased energy output for more efficient colonies.
[*] Enhanced Trading Outposts – Boost your resource management and economy.
[/list]
[h3]Game Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reworked enemy scaling and resource pacing to make difficulty progression more consistent.
[*] Buffs and nerfs to select weapons, perks, and enemy waves for improved game flow and strategic variety.
[/list]
[h3]UI & Quality of Life[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated menus and HUD for better readability and cleaner visuals.
[*] [Pause menu now correctly displays detailed information across all tabs, especially the Building tab.
[/list]
[h3]Weapon Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] All weapons have received an updated audio mix to ensure better in-game feedback and impact.
[*] 
[/list]
[h3]Building Polish[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted build sizes for the Droid Factory and Trading Outpost to improve placement.
[*] General polish pass on building visuals and construction feedback.
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the Building tab in the pause menu was not displaying correct values.
[*] Audio feedback updated for XP, Credit, and Crystal pickups.
[*] Fixed issue with Droid combat circle indicator not deactivating after deployment.
[/list]
Thanks again for all your feedback, suggestions, and support! We’re already working on what’s next. If you haven’t yet, join the conversation over on [url=https://discord.com/invite/FW6G9ZETsg]the Discord[/url] and help shape the future of the game.

notes.title: 4K Support, UI Improvements, and More Optimization
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week, I’ve continued my [b]optimization work[/b] and refreshed the [b]UI for the building menu and tutorial[/b]. These changes should make the game feel smoother, clearer, and more accessible to all players.

[h3]Full 4K Resolution Support[/h3]

Thanks to the optimizations I’ve been working on over the past few weeks, I’m thrilled to announce that [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] now [b]supports all screen resolutions up to 4K![/b]
This is a huge achievement, as I wasn’t sure I’d be able to implement full 4K support before release. Now, whether you’re playing on a [b]high-end monito[/b]r or a [b]lower-resolution setup[/b], the game will scale properly for a [b]better visual experience[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/890fba72895fe2a2e8fc081475c76a1ff4d83c3e.jpg[/img]

[h3]Tutorial UI Overhaul[/h3]

A major piece of [b]player feedback[/b] was that the tutorial text—previously placed [b]above the instructor Mech[/b]—was difficult to read.
I’ve now [b]relocated the tutorial text[/b] to a new, [b]clearer[/b] position, significantly improving readability and making it easier to follow the instructions.

[h3]Building Menu UI Redesign[/h3]

Another key improvement this week is a [b]redesigned build menu UI[/b]. Some players reported that the [b]mouse cursor position[/b] wasn’t aligning correctly with UI elements, causing [b]misclicks[/b] when selecting buildings.
To fix this, I:
[list]
[*] [b]Resolved the cursor misalignment issue[/b].
[*] [b]Redesigned the UI layout[/b] to make important information clearer.
[*] [b]Improved readability[/b] so players can make better building choices at a glance.
[/list]
These changes should make base-building feel [b]more intuitive and frustration-free![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/d65398f1eccd5adb72b8dbe31ef8a2b3dea84eb8.jpg[/img]

[h3]Continuing Optimization & Polish[/h3]

The focus remains on [b]fine-tuning the game[/b], ensuring it runs smoothly and feels great to play. Your [b]feedback[/b] has been invaluable in helping me prioritize improvements—so keep it coming!
If you haven’t already, [b]join the Discord[/b] to share your thoughts, report issues, or just chat with fellow players!

Thanks for reading, and see you next Week!

notes.title: Optimization, Polish, and the Joy of Digital Photography
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week, the pace of adding [b]new features[/b] has intentionally slowed down. Instead of introducing more mechanics from my backlog, I’ve been [b]focusing on testing, polishing, and optimizing[/b] the existing systems. This approach ensures that I don’t accidentally introduce new bugs or impact FPS performance negatively, especially as we get closer to release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/272c67dc4428a12446bfdb76030e9f1caea5974a.png[/img]

[h3]Optimization: Cutting What Doesn’t Add Enough Value[/h3]

A big part of this week’s work has been [b]hunting for FPS-impacting elements[/b] that don’t bring enough value to justify their performance cost. It’s a tough process—some of these features took a lot of time to develop, but with some distance, I can now evaluate whether they truly enhance the [b]gameplay, atmosphere, or overall experience[/b].

The goal is clear: [b]make the game run better[/b] while keeping the core experience [b]immersive and enjoyable[/b] for all players, including those on lower-spec computers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/9f8e0a097f055b87b486f8f9920be46e781bcac5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/d0d01f397f32e0b3274b5be3ae72610d5f4a888e.png[/img]

[h3]Photo Mode: A New Appreciation for the Worlds[/h3]

I’ve also found myself using the [b]Photo Mode[/b] more and more, sometimes stopping in the middle of a battle or after spending time building up my base just to capture a moment. This feature is turning out to be one of my favorites, and I hope others will enjoy it just as much.

Not only does [b]Photo Mode[/b] add a nice [b]change of pace[/b] between intense waves, but it also offers a new way to [b]explore and appreciate the worlds[/b]. Since it allows for [b]free camera movement[/b], players can see the landscapes from a fresh perspective—something that isn’t possible in the usual [b]top-down gameplay[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/618ed8d4462c7efe362fce7d1efc59a2d97d6f6c.png[/img]

[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]

With the focus on [b]polish and performance[/b], I’m making sure the game [b]feels great to play[/b] before adding new content. There’s still a lot to refine, and I’m excited to keep improving the experience.

If you haven’t yet, [b]join the Discord[/b] to share your feedback, ideas, or even some in-game photos—I’d love to see how you’re using Photo Mode!

Thanks for being part of the journey—see you next week!

notes.title: Steam Achievements, Polish, and Bug Fixes
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week, I’ve been focused on [b]adding Steam achievements[/b], [b]polishing existing gameplay[/b], [b]and fixing reported bugs[/b]. As we get closer to release, my priority is making Wave Defense: Trappist feel [b]stable[/b], [b]smooth[/b], and [b]satisfying[/b] to play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/97d61b0515dc8ed5527f1e33f35ba39b9ee11c04.png[/img]

[h3]Adding Steam Achievements[/h3]

Achievements are a great way to give players a sense of [b]progression and direction[/b], rewarding them for key milestones while also encouraging them to experiment with different playstyles. Whether it’s exploring new worlds, mastering combat strategies, or simply capturing beautiful moments in [b]Photo Mode[/b], achievements will offer both recognition and subtle hints toward activities players may not have considered.

I want these to feel [b]meaningful[/b], not just like a checklist, so I’m carefully designing them to enhance the overall experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/3973186e93dadca0f834ee7c0adb0a67b5ed1494.png[/img]

[h3]Polishing the Game vs. Adding More Features[/h3]

Right now, I’m putting more effort into [b]refining what’s already in the game[/b] rather than expanding systems or introducing new features. There’s a [b]huge backlog[/b] of ideas I want to implement in future updates, but the focus at this stage is making sure that what’s in the game [b]feels great to play[/b].

Every mechanic, UI element, and interaction should feel [b]intuitive[/b], [b]polished[/b], [b]and satisfying[/b]. The better the foundation, the more exciting it will be to expand on in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/ec3b850122f3a2819d78abbabc026bd211594342.png[/img]

[h3]Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements[/h3]

notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone, and Happy New Year![/h1]

It’s been a few weeks since my last update, but I haven’t really taken a break from developing [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]. Over the holiday period, we released the [b]second patch to the demo[/b], a major update focused on [b]optimization[/b] and the introduction of the [b]Photo Mode[/b].

We also did a deep dive into the [b]game’s music[/b], crafted by legendary electronic musicians [b]Joel Mul[/b]l and [b]Nima Khak[/b] (me!). If you haven’t already, check it out—it’s one of my favorite parts of the game!

This week, I’ve been working on a variety of updates, from [b]UI improvements[/b] and [b]new settings options[/b] to [b]tutorial revisions[/b] and bug fixes. Let’s dive into what’s new!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/25755edcc0edcd3baadf1a91ef7170de9849f6e7.png[/img]

[h3]UI Rework and HUD Improvements[/h3]

The game’s [b]HUD[/b] has been revamped with two main goals in mind:
[olist]
[*] [b]Minimizing screen clutter[/b], giving players more room to enjoy the world and action.
[*] [b]Clearer, faster access to key information[/b].
[/olist]
Here’s what’s changed:
[list]
[*] The [b]minimap[/b] is now circular, moved to the lower-right corner, and becomes semi-transparent when not hovered over.
[*] Stats and resource values have been moved to the [b]right side of the screen[/b], freeing up the lower center for a cleaner view.
[*] Added projected [b]credits and crystal gains[/b] from buildings after each wave, a feature requested by players.
[/list]
The [b]Pause Menu[/b] has also received a significant upgrade with four new tabs:
[olist]
[*] [b]Perks Overview:[/b] Displays perks selected at each XP level.
[*] [b]Mech and Weapon Stats:[/b] Shows detailed values for the current loadout, making it easier to see the effects of selected perks.
[*] [b]Building Breakdown:[/b] Offers an in-depth overview of all buildings and related stats, helping players make informed strategic decisions.
[*] [b]Photo Album:[/b] Players can view all the pictures they’ve taken in Photo Mode.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/7f124305f22412ec275ca9522503676d073472d5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/cba573b8691881270cb4029f665769978ea293dd.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/0a3b507d029c5dabbf4a20e6ed0c2d5bc693921b.png[/img]
[h3]Revised Tutorial and New Lore[/h3]

The tutorial has been reworked based on player feedback to feel [b]faster-paced[/b] and more intuitive. Additionally, I’ve added some [b]lore and background[/b] to explain why the player is in the Trappist system and the importance of collecting crystals. While I won’t spoil too much here, I’m excited to continue developing this aspect of the game and hope it adds depth to the overall experience.

[h3]New Settings for Performance Optimization[/h3]

To help players on lower-end computers, I’ve introduced a new [b]Downsampling option[/b] in the settings menu. This allows players to slightly lower the game’s graphics, which can significantly improve FPS without drastically affecting visuals. In my tests, even small adjustments made a noticeable difference. If you’re experiencing FPS drops, this is worth trying!

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]

Here are a few bugs that have been resolved in this update:
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where [b]photos taken in-world[/b] weren’t saving to players’ computers.
[*] Adjusted some [b]Photo Mode[/b] bugs for smoother operation.
[*] General stability and optimization fixes.
[/list]
[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]

It feels great to kick off 2025 with so many exciting updates and improvements already in place. As always, your feedback is invaluable, so keep it coming! Join the [b]Discord[/b] to share your thoughts, report bugs, and suggest new features—I’d love to hear from you.

Thank you for your support, and here’s to an amazing year ahead for [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]! See you next week!

notes.title: New Music, Mech Rework, and Weapon Overhaul
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week has been all about introducing some of the [b]big systems[/b] I’ve been planning for [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]. From music and mech improvements to a full weapon overhaul, there’s a lot to share! Let’s dive in.

[h3]New Music by Joel Mull[/h3]

As a music producer myself, sound design and music are a huge part of the world I want to create in [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]. That’s why I’m so thrilled to announce that [b]Joel Mull[/b], the world-renowned electronic music producer, has written and produced brand-new tracks specifically for the game.

The addition of Mull’s music is a game-changer, bringing a deeper atmosphere and energy to every battle, exploration, and build session. I’ll be dedicating a future update entirely to this topic, and hopefully, I can get Mull to share some of his thoughts directly with you all. Stay tuned—this is just the beginning of a much bigger story around the game’s music!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/b9b4deb5d6a60fa53ab3f8b8d80fe96dcd678f94.png[/img]

[h3]Mech Movement Rework with Inverse Kinematics[/h3]

One of the biggest changes this week is a full [b]rework of the Mech’s movement and animations[/b]. I’ve implemented [b]Inverse Kinematics[/b] (IK), which, without getting too technical, means the Mech’s movements are now far more realistic and dynamic.

Previously, the Mech’s weapon would simply spin in its hand when aiming, but now, the Mech’s entire body and arms move naturally as it adjusts to aim at different targets. This makes controlling the Mech feel much better, whether you’re walking, running, jetpacking, or shooting at enemies.

This system has been a lot of work to get in place, but I’m confident it makes a noticeable difference to the feel of the game. I’ll continue to refine and improve this system with each iteration, and I can’t wait to hear your feedback on how it feels.

[h3]Weapon Overhaul and New Weapon Stats[/h3]

The game’s weapons and weapon systems have received a major overhaul this week. Each weapon now has a distinct feel thanks to the introduction of a [b]Weapon Handling[/b] stat.

Some weapons, like the [b]Radioactive SMG[/b], are fast and nimble, while others, like the [b]Gatling Gun[/b], are harder to handle but deal massive damage. To give players an easier overview of weapon differences, each weapon now displays three core stats:
[list]
[*] [b]Damage[/b] – How much raw damage the weapon deals.
[*] [b]Handling[/b] – How easy and smooth the weapon is to use.
[*] [b]Efficiency[/b] – How resource-efficient the weapon is in battle.
[/list]
All weapons in the game have been rebalanced to reflect these changes, making them feel more unique and satisfying to use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/15eb46ac3775b35c95740e74897f5de8d1f35c42.png[/img]

[h3]New Weapon: The Staff Cannon[/h3]

I’m also excited to introduce a brand-new weapon: the [b]Staff Cannon[/b]. This will be an [b]endgame weapon[/b], designed to be both incredibly powerful and very fun to use. It’s perfect for players who want to bring some serious firepower to the battlefield!

At the same time, I’ve decided to [b]remove the Fire Bow[/b], as it no longer felt like it fit with the game’s overall design. And as a final touch, the [b]Flamethrower[/b] now has its proper weapon model, adding a polished look to one of the most satisfying weapons in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/cc880433080f455ecef801e3d08714855088d85e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/6a306e47505dea25ee47063104bcbc7f9efc1828.png[/img]

[h3]Bug Fixes and Miscellaneous Improvements[/h3]

Finally, here are some additional updates and fixes that went into the latest build:
[list]
[*] [b]Feedback Form Fixes:[/b] Resolved issues with the feedback form to ensure smoother player input.
[*] [b]Audio Mixer:[/b] Fixed a bug that caused the audio mixer to not work correctly when players were in the world.
[/list]
[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]

It’s been a busy but exciting week of development, and I feel like the game is moving closer to the vision I’ve always had for it. With new music, improved Mech animations, and a refined weapon system, [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] is shaping up to be more dynamic, immersive, and fun than ever.

As always, your feedback is invaluable, so please let me know what you think of the new changes. Join our [url=https://discord.gg/7TWAvkEA][b]Discord[/b][/url] to share your thoughts, report bugs, or suggest features you’d like to see in the game.

Thank you so much for your support—see you next Week!

[*] [b]Ionstrike Turret:[/b] A powerful long-range turret with a slow fire rate. It’s perfect for dealing massive damage from a distance, making it a great addition to your defense strategy.

notes.title: Walls, Watchtowers, and Rapid Improvements
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week, I’ve been continuing the work from last week with [b]rapid iterations[/b] and addressing issues highlighted during our recent playtesting sessions. It’s been incredibly rewarding to see both minor and major improvements coming into the game, each one helping [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] feel more polished and enjoyable.

Some of these changes are features I’ve wanted to add for a while but hadn’t quite figured out how to implement until now. A great example of this is the ability to [b]build walls[/b] around your base. With the latest build, I’ve finally introduced this feature, and I’m thrilled with how it’s turned out. Not only does it make your base feel more like a true stronghold, but it also adds a deeper sense of [b]control[/b] by letting you fortify your defenses and protect certain angles more effectively.

That’s just one of the improvements from this week—there’s a lot more to share!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/7974154385a5d0904a2eab708e65b88758f1e350.png[/img]

[h3]New Additions and Improvements:[/h3]

Here’s a full list of what’s been added and improved in the latest build:

[b]New Features:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]New Building – Walls:[/b] Players can now build walls around their base or wherever they want. Protect key structures and channel alien waves with strategic wall placement!
[*] [b]New Building – Watchtowers:[/b] Watchtowers extend the range of nearby turrets by 20%. Turrets near a Watchtower now display an indicator showing the boost.
[*] [b]Turrets Holo Shields:[/b]A new [b]Facility Upgrade[/b] available in the Mech Hangar, adding an extra layer of protection for your turrets.
[*] [b]Building Level Indicators:[/b] Buildings now show a [b]yellow star[/b] when they reach Max Level, with visual indicators added for Level 2 as well.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/50b4a8e1e3091226256b92dd72056ef69351c46a.png[/img]

[b]Quality-of-Life Improvements:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Quick Tips on Loading Pages:[/b] Useful gameplay tips now appear during loading screens. You can also find a full list of tips on the Start Page.
[*] [b]Camera Stability in Building Mode:[/b] The camera now remains fixed while in Building Mode, making it easier to place buildings precisely.
[*] [b]Multi-Build Functionality:[/b] Players can now build multiple copies of a structure without returning to the build menu. Use the right mouse button to exit Building Mode.
[*] [b]Artifact Collection:[/b] Artifacts now disappear after they’ve been collected, keeping the environment tidy and reducing confusion.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Facility Upgrade Station Bug:[/b] Fixed a bug where pressing ESC in the Facility Upgrade Station caused issues.
[*] [b]Turret Lighting Bug:[/b] Fixed an issue with turret lighting on certain maps.
[*] [b]Weather Volume Adjustment:[/b] Weather effects are now balanced to match other sound effects for a more cohesive audio experience.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/a7f9b8eebdc5d656ff2fde9456389dbd88701241.png[/img]

[h3]A Satisfying Week of Progress[/h3]

notes.title: Playtest Feedback, Game Settings, and Introducing Your New Companion
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

This week has been all about taking in the feedback from the ongoing playtests and making improvements to polish and refine [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]. While I haven’t received as much feedback as I was hoping for, the feedback I’ve gotten so far has been incredibly valuable. It’s already helping me fix some bugs and improve the overall quality of the game, and I’m excited to share what’s been worked on!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/d119f57ef48a86dcf3ed4a88ff77189e54ba019c.png[/img]

[h3]Feedback from Playtests: Polishing the Pause System[/h3]

One key issue reported by testers was the game’s [b]pause and unpause behavior[/b], which was acting strangely in certain scenarios. During my own testing, I tended to stick to the "Happy Path" (doing things as intended), so I never triggered these bugs myself. Thanks to the feedback, I was able to identify and rebuild the logic for how and when the game pauses.

The new system ensures the game will pause correctly when players:
[list]
[*] Open the map
[*] Receive an upgrade
[*] Send feedback or report a bug
[*] Interact with other menus or systems mid-game
[/list]

This rebuild has made the pause system much more robust and should feel much smoother and more intuitive for players. It’s a small but important improvement that enhances the polish and makes a better first impression for new players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/5ed49ef3d3d066a1c9660938fa45b02760b7d7a5.png[/img]

[h3]Improved Settings Accessibility[/h3]

Another area I’ve worked on this week is ensuring the [b]game settings[/b] work as intended at all stages of the game. Players can now adjust [b]audio[/b] and [b]visual settings[/b] seamlessly, whether they’re in:
[list]
[*] The Start Menu
[*] The Mech Construction Hub
[*] Mid-game while deployed on a new world
[/list]

This change makes it easier for players to customize their experience without interruptions, no matter where they are in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/d41fb2bec2b767054ccf4badd09df5ba7769e7f1.png[/img]

[h3]Introducing the Companion Drone[/h3]

The biggest and most exciting addition this week is the new [b]Companion Drone[/b] that will join your Mech on every planet. This little helper brings a host of improvements to the game’s mechanics and emotional experience. Here’s what the drone does:
[list]
[*] [b]Automatic Combat Support[/b]: The drone replaces the Mech’s old "passive auto weapon" system. It will now automatically target and shoot at aliens within its range, adding a more dynamic and engaging feel to combat.
[*] [b]Artifact Scanning[/b]: Instead of the Mech’s backpack holding scanning tools, the drone will now be responsible for scanning and detecting [b]Artifacts[/b] as you explore new worlds. This makes much more sense visually and thematically.
[*] [b]Building and Upgrading Structures[/b]: When constructing or upgrading buildings, the drone will handle the physical construction instead of structures simply appearing. This small change adds a lot of immersion and polish to the base-building process.
[/list]

[b]Not Just a Helper, but a Friend[/b]

One of the things I love most about the drone is the emotional element it adds. Landing on a new planet used to feel a little lonely, especially before your base was set up. Now, with the drone by your side, you’ve got a companion to share the adventure with from the start.

But there’s one thing still missing: [b]a name[/b]! I’d love to hear your ideas for what to call the drone. Join our Discord and share your suggestions—I’m excited to see what you all come up with!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/26ef89a1362aa48950052ab641b3fc5c9d981576.png[/img]

[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]

This week has been all about improving polish, fixing bugs, and adding new features based on feedback. In the coming weeks, I’ll be continuing to refine the gameplay experience, gather more feedback from playtesters, and prepare for the open demo in December.

As always, I’d love to hear your thoughts and suggestions! If you’re playing the beta, please share your feedback in the Discord. And don’t forget to send in your name ideas for the drone—I can’t wait to see what you come up with!

Thanks for reading, and see you next week!

notes.title: Beta Testing Begins – Economy Balancing, Tutorial Updates, and Leaderboards
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

Exciting news this week as [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] has officially entered [b]beta testing[/b]! We’ve opened up the playtest for new players to join through our Discord, and it’s been fantastic to see the first players jump in, explore the game, and start sharing feedback. Over the coming weeks, we’ll progressively add more players until the [b]open demo[/b] launches in December, when anyone will be able to try out the game on Steam.

In the meantime, here’s a look at what I’ve been working on this week based on early feedback, plus a few new features to make the experience even better!

[h3]Balancing the In-Game Economy[/h3]

A balanced economy is key to making the gameplay experience both challenging and satisfying, so I’ve been focusing on [b]fine-tuning the in-game economy[/b] to ensure players have a smooth start when they begin building their first base. This work involves adjusting resource generation, costs, and availability to create a fair balance between challenge and opportunity.

As the playtesting continues, I’ll be monitoring player feedback and data to make sure the economy feels right, both in the early game and as players progress. I’m looking forward to refining this even further with the insights we get from testers.

[h3]Strengthening the Tutorial[/h3]

The [b]Tutorial[/b] is essential for introducing new players to the game’s mechanics, and based on initial feedback, I’ve reworked several of its systems to make it more robust and user-friendly. A few players ran into bugs during the tutorial that disrupted their experience, so I’ve implemented a new system that should address these issues.

The updated tutorial should now give players a smoother, more stable introduction to the game’s core mechanics. I’m eager to see how the changes work out with new players and will keep iterating based on feedback to make sure everyone has a positive first experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/a76d0c2e1a2a66e3e2b05811691535c71c6cf943.png[/img]

[h3]Join the Playtest and Share Your Feedback![/h3]

I’m excited to keep expanding the beta testing group and gathering feedback to make [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] the best experience it can be. If you’re interested in joining the playtest, hop into the [b]Discord[/b] to request access, and be sure to [b]wishlist the game on Steam[/b] to stay up to date with the upcoming open demo in December.

notes.title: The Final Boss Fight, UI Updates, and Upcoming Demo
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

Welcome back to another dev blog for [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]! This week has been packed with exciting work on the game’s [b]endgame content[/b], specifically the [b]final boss fight[/b] that players will encounter after navigating the path of worlds we talked about last week. I’ve also been tackling some [b]UI adjustments[/b] to improve the base-building experience based on feedback, and I’m thrilled to announce a demo coming in December!

[h3]The Final Boss Fight: The Ultimate Challenge[/h3]

When players reach the end of the [b]procedural map[/b] and overcome all the challenges along the way, they’ll be met with one last, ultimate test—the [b]final boss fight[/b]. This encounter is designed to feel very different from the other worlds and battles players have experienced. Here’s what makes it unique:
[list]
[*]  [b]No Base-Building[/b]: Unlike the other worlds, where players build and defend a base, the boss fight throws players straight into a head-on battle. You’ll be up against a new [b]boss alien[/b] that’s significantly stronger and more challenging than any enemies you’ve encountered before.
[*] [b]Waves of Previous Enemies[/b]: To raise the stakes even further, waves of previously defeated aliens will also join the fray. This final battle will test not only your [b]Mech Build[/b] but also your [b]Mech Piloting skills[/b] under intense pressure.
[*] [b]Permanent Defeat[/b]: One key difference here is that you don’t have a [b]Mission Control[/b] building in this battle, which means if your mech is destroyed, it’s game over for that run. There’s no reassembly—only a definitive challenge to see how far your build and skills can take you.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/a99e69ceb488005cc627dc50f2951bc0a2901773.png[/img]

Designing this boss and creating new abilities and attacks that feel fresh and impactful has been a really fun process. I can’t wait to see how players react to this final showdown and what strategies they bring to the fight!

[h3]UI and Base-Building Mechanics Improvements[/h3]

In addition to the final boss, I’ve also been working on refining the [b]UI and mechanics for base-building[/b]. Recently, several playtesters shared feedback that the base-building interface could feel a bit overwhelming, with too much information shown at once. Another issue was the accidental [b]one-click building upgrades[/b]—players sometimes upgraded buildings without meaning to, which could disrupt their strategy and resource management.

To address this feedback, I’ve made two key changes:
[list]
[*] [b]Condensed Building Info[/b]: Now, when you hover over a building, you’ll see a more streamlined summary. For the full details, you just need to right-click on the building. This change keeps the UI cleaner and more intuitive, while still providing in-depth information when you need it.
[*] [b]Upgrade Confirmation[/b]: Instead of a single button press, upgrading a building now requires you to [b]hold down the button[/b] for a few moments. This should prevent accidental upgrades and give players a bit more control over their decisions.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/ef8a2fb4cc1e00c940465f3f480266195698246a.png[/img]

These changes were designed to make the base-building experience feel more accessible and intuitive, and I’m eager to hear what players think about the updates.

[h3]Demo in December![/h3]

Now for some big news: with my friends at Caketown, who are publishing the game, we’ve decided to release a demo in December! My focus over the next few weeks will be to polish and stabilize the game to ensure a smooth, satisfying experience for everyone who will try it.

The demo will of course be available here on [b]Steam[/b], so if you’re interested in joining, make sure to [b]wishlist the game[/b] and join the [b]Discord[/b] to stay up to date with all the details. This is a great opportunity to try the game firsthand, share your feedback, and be part of shaping [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i].

However, if you can’t wait for the demo?! Check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3014930/view/4512136358584647763?l=english]this post[/url] on how to become an early MECH, joining the beta tester channel on Discord.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/604adeb2c873d596487b4e147dc10ba96152cb32.png[/img]

[h3]Looking Forward[/h3]

The upcoming weeks will be focused on refining the demo and improving stability. I’m incredibly excited to see new players jump into the game and share their experiences, and I look forward to making any improvements based on your feedback.

Thank you for following along with the journey, and I hope to see many of you in the playtesting session! As always, feel free to share your thoughts, ideas, or questions in the comments or on Discord.

notes.title: Choose Your Path – Feedback, and Procedural Progression
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

It’s been an exciting week for [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i], as I’ve finally had the chance to take full advantage of the [b]optimizations[/b] I’ve been working on for the past few weeks. Along with some valuable feedback from a professional level-designer and new developments on player progression, I’m excited to share what’s been going on behind the scenes!

[h3]Alien Horde Battles: Optimizations Paying Off[/h3]

Over the past few weeks, I’ve been working hard to optimize memory usage and improve the game’s overall performance. This week, I was able to really see the benefits of those optimizations in action. So far, I’ve been able to [b]spawn up to three times as many alien AI[/b] during attacks on the base without any significant impact on performance, which is a huge win.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/a35ed3b24dc14f14e0c97c195ec75bbdea0ecbc1.png[/img]

What this means for gameplay is that the battles will feel a lot more [b]intense[/b] and chaotic, creating a true [b]horde feeling[/b] when waves of aliens start to attack. The ability to spawn more enemies ramps up the [b]challenge[/b] and really pushes the player’s defenses and strategy to their limits. I’m excited to keep testing this and see just how far I can push the scale of these battles without impacting performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/992a5767888eecaedab67906678ce77ff657b0a4.png[/img]

[h3]Professional Feedback and Level Design Improvements[/h3]

This week, I also had the chance to sit down with a friend who is a [b]senior level designer[/b] with many years of experience in the game industry. Her feedback has been incredibly valuable, and I’m looking forward to implementing some of the changes she suggested in the coming weeks.

While I can’t reveal all the details just yet, I’m confident that her insights will help [b]raise the overall quality and experience[/b] of the game. I’ll be revisiting some of the worlds and level designs with her feedback in mind, and I’m really excited to see how these changes enhance the gameplay experience. Stay tuned for more updates on this in the near future!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/816015c9ed7e85bb31d55dc8c2addb874c0ea9d8.png[/img]

[h3]Choose Your Path: Procedural Progression System[/h3]

The main focus of my work this week has been on implementing a new system that allows players to [b]choose their own path[/b] between worlds. This feature is still a work in progress, but I’m excited to share a sneak peek of how it’s shaping up.

I’ve attached a [b]screenshot of the prototype[/b] for this system, where players will be able to select different paths leading up to a [b]boss fight[/b] at the end. Along the way, players will encounter different types of worlds, each with its own challenges and rewards. These paths and rewards will be [b]procedurally generated[/b] for each run, ensuring that every playthrough feels unique.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/7a9a1b432830e32a6ee0a2cc63b83ff040c875e7.png[/img]

The goal with this system is to add a layer of [b]strategic decision-making[/b] to the game, giving players the freedom to choose their own journey. Depending on which path you take, you’ll encounter different enemies, earn different rewards, and face different obstacles. I hope this will not only make each run feel fresh and exciting but also add a lot of [b]replayability[/b] to the game as players experiment with different paths and strategies.

[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]

I’m excited about where the game is heading, and there’s still plenty of work to do. Next on the list is refining the [b]path selection system[/b], continuing to implement the feedback I received on level design, and pushing the limits of enemy spawns even further. The optimizations from the past few weeks have really opened up a lot of possibilities for the game’s future.

As always, I’d love to hear your thoughts! How do you feel about having the freedom to choose your path through the worlds? What kind of rewards or challenges do you think would make this system even more engaging? Let me know in the comments or on Discord—I’m always eager to hear your feedback!

Thanks for reading, and see you next week!

By optimizing the game now, I’m setting the stage for [b]faster iteration[/b] in the future. It will be much easier to test out new game design ideas, add new features, and tweak existing systems without worrying about performance hits or memory issues.

In essence, I’m laying a solid foundation that will allow me to be more [b]experimental and agile[/b] going forward. As a solo developer, being able to quickly test and iterate on ideas is key to finding what works best for the game.

[h3]Looking Ahead: More Intense Battles[/h3]

I’m really excited about what these optimizations will allow me to do in the near future. One of the first things I want to test out is [b]increasing the number of aliens in each wave[/b]. As the game’s performance improves, I should be able to push the battle intensity further by having more enemies spawn at once, creating bigger, more chaotic fights that challenge the player even more.

This will make the waves feel more intense and give players a greater sense of accomplishment when they successfully defend their base against a larger swarm of enemies. I’m looking forward to seeing how the game feels once I can test these changes in action!

[h3]A Shorter Update This Week[/h3]

I know this is a shorter update compared to some of the previous dev blogs, but a lot of this week’s work has been behind the scenes, continuing the efforts from last week. I’m excited to push forward with these optimizations and start testing out what they enable for the gameplay itself in the coming weeks.

As always, thanks for following along with the development of [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i]! I can’t wait to share more with you next week, and I’d love to hear any thoughts or suggestions you have. notes.title: Garbage Collection, Autumn Cleaning, and Shooting Animations
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

Welcome back to another update on the development of [i]Wave Defense: Trappist![/i] This week has been a busy one, with a focus on improving the game’s performance, doing some "autumn cleaning" of old assets, and polishing up the [b]shooting animations[/b]. Let’s dive into what’s been going on!

[h3]Tackling Garbage Collection and Loading Times[/h3]

As [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] has grown, I’ve noticed that the [b]loading times[/b] have been getting longer, especially when starting up the game. This was becoming a bit of a concern, so I decided it was time to dig into what was causing the delays.

After investigating, I found that some objects were causing [b]memory leaks[/b], which were contributing to the extended loading times. This was a new area for me, so I spent a good amount of time reading up and watching tutorials on how to use tools like the [b]Memory Profiler[/b] to better understand what was happening under the hood.

With the insights gained, I started implementing changes aimed at optimizing how memory is used, ensuring that unnecessary objects are properly cleaned up—essentially working on better [b]garbage collection[/b]. While I haven't solved everything yet, I’m happy to report that the loading times have been cut in half compared to before. This feels like a solid achievement for this iteration, and I’ll continue refining it to make sure everything runs as smoothly as possible.

[h3]Autumn Cleaning: Tidying Up the Scenes[/h3]

While working on the loading times, I took the opportunity to do some [b]autumn cleaning[/b] across all of my game scenes. Over time, I’ve tested countless game objects, 3D models, and snippets of code, many of which ended up not being used in the final version of the game. Even though these objects were turned off, they were still lingering in the scenes, adding unnecessary complexity.

So, I rolled up my sleeves and went through every scene to [b]delete and clean up[/b] anything that wasn’t needed anymore. This kind of maintenance work might not sound glamorous, but it’s incredibly important. Removing unused assets reduces clutter and makes the game more efficient, while also making future updates and iterations much easier to manage. It feels good to have everything cleaned up, and I’m already noticing how much smoother it is to work on the project now.

[h3]Shooting Animations: Adding That Extra Polish[/h3]

Another highlight of this week has been working on [b]shooting and reloading animations[/b] for most of the weapons in the game. This has actually been one of the more fun tasks I’ve taken on recently. Animations can make such a big difference in terms of how the game feels, and I wanted to ensure that the shooting mechanics in [i]Wave Defense: Trappist[/i] are as satisfying as possible. 

[previewyoutube=ZaduGFIrKgw;full][/previewyoutube]

With some trial and error, and the help of a few animation tools, I’ve managed to create and adjust the shooting animations for different weapons. The goal was to make the weapons feel impactful—every shot should come with a sense of recoil, moving your mech slightly, and giving each weapon a unique "kick." I think these subtle touches really add to the overall polish of the game, making combat more immersive and visually engaging.

[previewyoutube=1WmCkm80hq8;full][/previewyoutube]

I’m definitely no expert when it comes to animation, but I was surprised by how accessible the process could be once I got the hang of it. By experimenting and learning along the way, I’ve been able to add a layer of refinement that I hope players will notice and appreciate.

[h3]Wrapping Up the Week[/h3]

This week has been all about [b]optimization, cleaning, and polish[/b]—cutting down loading times, clearing out old clutter, and adding some final touches to animations that bring the mechs and their weapons to life. It’s been a challenging but satisfying process, and I’m excited to keep building on this progress.

Thanks for reading, and see you next Week!

notes.title: Making Your Mech Truly Yours – Customization in Wave Defense: Trappist
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

Welcome back to another dev blog for Wave Defense: Trappist! This week, I want to talk about a feature I’m really excited about—how you can make your mech feel truly personal. Customization is a big part of the game, and I’ve spent a lot of time working on ways to ensure that your mech reflects your playstyle and personality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/0ad547d58b318e66e2ca5021cebddf089f7f04b3.jpg[/img]
[h3]Customization Beyond Weapons[/h3]
In Wave Defense: Trappist, your mech is your main tool for surviving the waves of alien enemies and gathering precious Crystals. While players will have the ability to equip and modify various [b]weapon systems[/b]—a topic I’ll dive into in a future blog—there’s another layer of customization that I think will really resonate with players: the ability to [b]paint and customize the appearance of your mech[/b].

With an [b]infinite number of spray cans[/b], endless[b] color options[/b], and a wide variety of [b]brushes[/b], players can spend as much or as little time as they want designing their mech’s look. Want to slap on a quick color change before heading into battle? Easy. Prefer to spend hours perfecting a detailed, multi-colored design? Go for it! You’ll be able to [b]save your paint jobs[/b], meaning that you can return to your favorite designs again and again—or try something new each time.
I believe that this is going to be a feature many players will appreciate. In fact, I wouldn’t be surprised if some players end up spending more time painting their mechs than venturing out into new worlds to gather Crystals!

[h3]The Challenge of Developing Fine-Grained Customization[/h3]
From a development perspective, this has been one of the more difficult features to implement. The core idea sounds simple—let players paint their mechs—but offering the kind of fine-grained control I wanted for this feature was much more complex than I initially thought.

I spent a lot of time researching different ways this could be implemented, from [b]real-time texture mapping[/b] to creating a system that allows for true [b]brush-like precision[/b]. I wanted players to feel like they could really take ownership of their mech’s design, whether they were going for a sleek, monochromatic look or an intricate, layered design.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/88ec40b099f2b7ef7e85490415bbd834382513d7.png[/img]
Early iterations didn’t give the player the control I was aiming for. The painting tools were too simplistic, and it didn’t feel like the kind of customization experience I wanted for Wave Defense: Trappist. After testing several different approaches, I landed on a system that finally gives players the level of control they need to really make their mechs their own. There’s still room to iterate and improve, and I’m excited to see how players respond to this feature once they get their hands on it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/7126e7519e421b59e7357106ef17b06655de538d.png[/img]
[h3]Designing a Fun and Accessible UI[/h3]
Another big challenge with this feature has been creating a [b]UI[/b] that’s both [b]accessible[/b] and [b]fun to use[/b]. I want the painting process to feel intuitive, so players aren’t struggling with the controls, but also deep enough that players who want to invest more time into customizing their mechs have the tools they need.

I’ve gone through several iterations of the UI, testing different layouts and control schemes to find something that works for a wide range of players. Whether you’re using a mouse and keyboard or a gamepad, the painting system should feel natural and responsive. That said, the UI is something I’m sure I’ll continue to tweak as more feedback rolls in. Your input will be invaluable in helping me fine-tune this feature, so I’m looking forward to seeing how you all engage with it.

[h3]Why Personalization Matters[/h3]
Giving players the ability to customize their mechs is about more than just aesthetics—it’s about letting them [b]express themselves[/b] in the game. I want players to feel connected to their mechs, and one of the best ways to do that is by giving them the tools to make their mech look exactly how they want it to. It’s your mech, your way, and I’m really excited to see the creative designs that players come up with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/0c7dcb2ee48ddb5f70656378b380df12884f8831.png[/img]
Let me know in the comments or over on Discord—I can’t wait to see the creativity this community brings to the game.

[b]Thanks for reading, and see you next Week![/b]

notes.title: Crafting the New Player Experience in Wave Defense: Trappist
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

I’m back with another update on the development of Wave Defense: Trappist. This week, I’ve been focusing on something really important—the [b]new player experience[/b]. As a developer, one of my biggest goals is to make the game as accessible and enjoyable as possible for new players, while still retaining its depth and complexity for those who want to dig deeper.

While Wave Defense: Trappist is designed to be easy to pick up and play, it also has some layers of complexity. Between piloting your mech, managing the in-game economy, building your base, exploring different worlds, finding artifacts, and navigating the roguelike meta progression, there’s quite a bit to learn. So, this week, I’ve been experimenting with different ways to make the onboarding process smoother and more intuitive.

[h3]The First Approach: In-Game Tips[/h3]
Initially, I wanted to keep things minimal and non-intrusive. My first idea was to provide notifications that would appear during a regular run. These [b]notifications[/b] would give players hints and tips as they played, offering guidance on how to use the game’s systems.

However, after testing this approach with a few friends who hadn’t played the game before, I quickly realized it wasn’t working as well as I had hoped. When you’re being attacked by waves of aliens, having text pop up with helpful tips can be overwhelming—too much to process at once! Players found it difficult to absorb the information while also trying to survive the chaos of combat.

[h3]Going Back to the Drawing Board[/h3]
After seeing how hard it was for new players to catch on with the in-game tips approach, I decided to take a step back and really think through what new players need to know to have a good time in Wave Defense: Trappist.

I mapped out all of the key systems and mechanics they’d need to understand: how to pilot the mech effectively, base-building basics, understanding the in-game economy, what to expect from alien attacks, and even the roguelike elements like meta progression. Once I had everything laid out, it became clear that a more structured introduction was necessary.

[b]The Solution: Tutorial World[/b]
With this in mind, I decided to create a completely new [b]Tutorial World[/b]. This will be the first stop for every new player when they start their first run. In this environment, players are introduced to the game in a more controlled, less stressful setting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/712a16211249b81c6a7e205f35d58b675f00412f.png[/img]
[h3]Here’s how it works:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Meet the Instructor: In Tutorial World, players are greeted by an instructor who guides them through the key mechanics. This guide will walk players through the basics of the HUD, show them how to place down buildings, and provide a solid introduction to the in-game economy and resource management.
[*] First Taste of Combat: Players will even experience their first alien wave attack in a low-pressure environment. This gives them a chance to test out their mech’s weapons and get comfortable with how combat works before the real challenges begin.
[*] Mech Construction Hangar: Once the basics are covered, players will be introduced to the Mech Construction Hangar, where they’ll learn about meta progression and how they can improve their mech between runs. This part of the tutorial will be a deep dive into customizing and upgrading their mech—something I’ll go into more detail about in a future blog!
[*] First Run: After completing the tutorial, players are sent off on their first mission—essentially a normal run—armed with the knowledge they need to tackle the game’s systems and survive the alien onslaught.
[/list]

[h3]Iterating on the Experience[/h3]
Of course, this is just the beginning. I’m going to continue testing and iterating on the [b]Tutorial World[/b] to make sure it strikes the right balance between being informative and engaging. There’s always room for improvement, and I want to ensure that new players feel confident and excited when they start their journey through the Trappist system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45097607/fa9ceb2f5c980a5598280bdfef2aaf1771bd9105.png[/img]
[h3]Why This Matters[/h3]
Getting the new player experience right is crucial for any game, especially one with as many moving parts as Wave Defense: Trappist. By offering a smooth introduction to the game’s mechanics, I hope to reduce any barriers to entry and help players hit the ground running. I’m really excited about the progress so far, and I think this new approach will help players better understand the game and feel more connected to their mechs and their strategies from the start.

As always, I’d love to hear your thoughts! How do you feel about the new [b]Tutorial World[/b] approach? Are there any specific mechanics or systems you think should be explained in more detail? Let me know in the comments or on Discord.

Thanks for reading, and see you next week!

notes.title: Behind the Scenes – Redesigning Base-Building in Wave Defense: Trappist
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

Welcome back to the third dev blog for Wave Defense: Trappist. Today, I want to take you behind the scenes of development and give you a glimpse of the redesign process that’s currently underway. As a solo developer, I’m constantly iterating on ideas, testing mechanics, and rethinking how the game plays to ensure it’s both fun and challenging. Lately, I’ve been focused on redesigning one of the game’s core mechanics: [b]base-building[/b].

[h3]The Old System: Limited Placement[/h3]
When I first started working on Wave Defense: Trappist, the base-building system was fairly rigid. The player could only construct buildings in specific locations that I had predetermined. I would place markers across the map, and each marker had a designated building type that could be constructed there. While this gave me a lot of control over the layout and pacing of each level, it also felt a bit restrictive for the player.

Many of you have expressed an interest in having more freedom to choose how and where you build your base, and I totally agree that this would add a whole new layer of strategy to the game. After all, one of the joys of a game like this is the ability to experiment with different setups and playstyles.

[h3]The New System: Player Freedom with Base-Building[/h3]
So I’ve been hard at work redesigning the base-building system to give you more control. In this new version, you’ll be able to build any facility—whether it’s a Power Plant, Trade Post, Droid Factory, or Manufacturing Plant—wherever you see fit. This gives you the freedom to craft your own strategies based on the situation at hand.

Want to create a heavily fortified zone around your Mission Control Facility? Go for it. Prefer to spread out your structures and create smaller, more specialized outposts? That’s also an option! The choice is yours, and I can’t wait to see the creative ways players will experiment with base layouts.

[h3]Challenges: Pathfinding and Balancing Freedom[/h3]
Of course, with more freedom comes more complexity, and this redesign isn’t without its challenges. One of the biggest hurdles I’m facing right now is [b]enemy pathfinding[/b]. In the previous system, the AI always knew exactly how to get to your buildings because they were in fixed, predictable locations. Now that the player has more freedom to build anywhere, there’s a risk that enemies might not be able to find their way to certain structures, making them impossible to attack.

This would create an unintentional loophole where players could potentially place important structures in “safe zones” that are unreachable by enemies, breaking the balance of the game.

[h3][/h3]The Current Solution: Restricted Building Zones
To solve this, I’m implementing a system where areas that enemies can’t pathfind to will be marked as [b]restricted zones[/b] for building. These zones will appear as visually distinct areas, and the player won’t be able to place any structures there. Outside of these restricted zones, though, you’ll have complete freedom to build anywhere you want. This way, we maintain the challenge of defending your base from enemy attacks while still giving you a lot more flexibility in how you set things up.

[h3]Iterating and Testing[/h3]
This kind of redesign is an iterative process, and I’m currently in the thick of testing different configurations. I’m tweaking the AI to ensure they can still navigate the environment and attack effectively, while also fine-tuning the balance to make sure that base-building feels fun and strategic without giving players too much of an advantage.

Another thing I’m focusing on is making sure the user interface for this new system is clear and easy to use. Building should feel intuitive, and restricted zones need to be obvious enough that players can immediately understand why certain areas are off-limits without disrupting the flow of the game.

[h3]What’s Next?[/h3]
Moving forward, I’ll be continuing to test and refine this new system, but I’m excited about the direction it’s heading in. Giving players the freedom to design their base layouts opens up so many new strategic possibilities, and I believe it’s going to make base-building one of the most engaging aspects of Wave Defense: Trappist.

As always, I’d love to hear your feedback! How do you feel about having more freedom in base-building? What challenges or opportunities do you think this will present? [b]Let me know in the comments or on Discord—I’m always eager to hear your thoughts![/b]

notes.title: Mastering Base-Building in Wave Defense: Trappist
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hey everyone![/b][/h1]

I’m back with another dev blog, and today I’m excited to dive into one of the most strategic aspects of Wave Defense: Trappist—base-building. Whether you’re fending off relentless alien waves or strategically mining precious resources, your base is the heart of your operations. Let’s take a closer look at how you’ll establish and fortify your base in the Trappist solar system.

[h2]Building Your Base: Mission Control Facility[/h2]

Every new world you land on begins with constructing your [b]Mission Control Facility.[/b] This building is the nerve center of your base, and it’s crucial to protect it at all costs. If your Mission Control Facility falls, your current run is over, so prioritizing its defense is key to survival.

But it’s not just about defense. The Mission Control Facility also generates Credits, the game’s primary currency, and unlocks [b]Building Zones.[/b] As you upgrade this facility, more Building Zones become available, giving you space to expand your base with additional structures.

[h2]Critical Facilities and Their Functions[/h2]

As you develop your base, you’ll have access to various facilities, each with a unique role. Here’s a rundown of what you’ll be working with:

[list]
[*] [b]Power Plant:[/b] This facility is the backbone of your base’s energy production. Every other facility relies on energy to function, so running out of power can be catastrophic. Defensive turrets will stop firing, and resource production will grind to a halt. Ensuring a stable energy supply is essential, so consider building and upgrading Power Plants early on. 
[*] [b]Droid Factory:[/b] The Droid Factory produces droids that assist in base defense. These droids can either follow you around or guard specific areas. However, the Droid Factory is a power-hungry facility, so make sure you have a solid energy infrastructure in place before constructing it. 
[*] [b]Trade Post:[/b] The Trade Post is a vital economic hub for your base. It converts harvested resources into Credits by trading with off-world markets. These Credits are crucial for building and upgrading your other facilities. As you upgrade the Trade Post, you can increase trading capacity, improve trade rates, and unlock specialized trade missions, all of which enhance your economic growth. 
[*] [b]Mining Facility:[/b] Crystals are the most valuable resource in Wave Defense: Trappist. Mining Facilities harvest these crystals from patches you discover on each world. The Crystals serve as the main meta-currency, allowing you to make permanent upgrades to your Mechs and other facilities. Like the Droid Factory, Mining Facilities consume a lot of energy, so be prepared to invest in your power grid if you want to maximize Crystal production. 
[*] [b]Laser Turrets:[/b] These defensive structures are your first line of defense against alien waves. Laser Turrets automatically target and attack any enemies within range, making them indispensable for keeping your base secure. Placement and upgrading of Laser Turrets will be critical in holding back the increasingly challenging waves of enemies.
[/list]


[h2]Strategic Upgrades[/h2]

Each facility can be upgraded using Credits, and these upgrades will enhance their effectiveness in different ways:

[list] [*] [b]Power Plants[/b] will produce more energy and become more efficient, reducing their vulnerability to enemy attacks.
 [*] [b]Droid Factories[/b] will increase the number of droids they produce and unlock advanced droid types. 
[*] [b]Trade Posts[/b] will increase trading capacity, improve trade rates, and unlock specialized missions. 
[*] [b]Mining Facilities[/b] will improve the rate at which they harvest Crystals and increase their energy efficiency. 
[*] [b]Laser Turrets[/b] will get a boost in range, damage, and rate of fire, making them even more deadly against incoming threats. [/list]

These upgrades allow you to tailor your base to your preferred playstyle and the unique challenges of each world you explore.

[h2]Balancing Defense and Resource Management[/h2]

One of the core challenges in Wave Defense: Trappist is finding the right balance between defending your base and expanding your economy. Building too many defensive structures might leave you without enough resources to upgrade your facilities, while focusing too much on resource production could leave you vulnerable to enemy attacks. Every decision counts, and the strategic depth of base-building is something I’m really excited for you all to experience.

In the next dev blog, I’ll be discussing the waves of enemies you’ll face and the strategic gameplay involved in fending them off. Until then, I’d love to hear how you plan to structure your base. Will you focus on strong defenses or a robust economy? Let me know in the comments or over on Discord!

As always, don’t forget to join our community to stay up to date with the latest news and connect with fellow players. Thanks for reading, and see you next Wednesday!

[b]If you want to get a closer look and talk directly to me, join my Discord![/b]
